sources.title: Electronic Visa
sources.publisher: Consulate General of the Republic of Iraq in Los Angeles, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Iraqi Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular page directs applicants to the official Iraqi electronic-visa platform. It does not identify Israeli passports or return an Israeli ordinary-passport eligibility decision.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Apply for an entry visa to Iraq electronically through the Iraqi electronic visa platform.

sources.title: GEN 1.3 — Entry, Transit and Departure of Passengers and Crew
sources.publisher: Syrian General Authority of Civil Aviation
sources.officialityEvidence: The live official Syrian electronic aeronautical-information publication states its GEN 1.3 passenger rule is effective 27 March 2026. It requires an advance visa unless exempt, but publishes no Israeli-passport mapping or eVisa issuance route.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Entry visa obtained in advance from a Syrian diplomatic mission, unless exempt.

sources.title: Foreign Ministry: no changes to entry procedures for arrivals
sources.publisher: Syrian Arab News Agency reporting the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates
sources.officialityEvidence: The live state-news publication reports the Foreign Ministry's 29 April 2026 confirmation that the entry procedures under Decision No. 128 of 1 July 2025 remain in force. It does not publish the decision's Israeli-passport treatment.
sources.supportingExcerpt: إن الإجراءات المعتمدة في دخول سوريا لا تزال سارية المفعول وفق القرار رقم 128

sources.title: Types of Visas
sources.publisher: Immigration, Passports and Nationality Authority, Ministry of Interior
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Yemen Immigration, Passports and Nationality Authority portal identifies the physical embassy-or-consulate sticker issued after Authority approval. It does not publish an Israeli ordinary-passport eligibility or approval decision.
sources.supportingExcerpt: The visa sticker is issued to foreigners by the embassies and consulates of the Republic abroad

unresolved.reason: Iran's MFA eVisa endpoint could not be replayed: it issued a self-referential HTTP 307 redirect until the client limit. No other accessible current Iranian government or controlling legal source directly maps an ordinary Israeli passport to a visitor route, a prohibition, or a decision/issuance process. No portal, diplomatic-relations or omission inference is made.

The live Iraqi Foreign Ministry page establishes only that an electronic-visa platform exists; it does not directly identify an Israeli ordinary passport or return an Israeli eligibility and issuance result. The national eVisa instructions also expose only a country-and-passport-type search, not an affirmative Israeli result. No federal-Iraq route, entry restriction, or ordinary visitor issuance timing is established from portal availability or omission.

Kuwait's live Ministry of Interior visa portal was reachable, but it exposed no reproducible Israeli-passport nationality rule, entry prohibition, or ordinary visitor issuance decision. No current accessible Kuwaiti government or controlling legal text directly maps an Israeli ordinary passport. The portal's availability, any selector omission, diplomatic relations and third-country or residence programmes are not used as evidence.

Lebanon's General Security nationality-entry material did not yield reproducible content in current replays. No accessible current Lebanese government or controlling legal text directly maps an Israeli ordinary passport to a visitor route, an entry prohibition, or a conditional authorization regime. Generic visitor rules and country-list omission are not an Israeli-passport determination.

Current Syrian Government material says Decision No. 128 remains in force and separately states that an advance visa is needed unless exempt, but neither source directly maps an Israeli ordinary passport, states an Israeli entry prohibition, or establishes electronic issuance. The fallback evisa label is therefore unverified and cannot be replaced with visa_required or a prohibition from a generic rule or an omitted nationality.

Yemen's live Immigration, Passports and Nationality Authority portal describes an Authority-approved physical visa sticker issued by an embassy or consulate, not an electronic visa. It does not directly map an Israeli ordinary passport to eligibility, a prohibition, an exceptional authorization, or pre-travel issuance. The fallback visa_required label is consequently unverified; portal availability and nationality omission are not used as a result.
